subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or reject the tool call instead?
rationale: The issue allows either warning or error, and fail-closed behavior would change the sandboxed exec contract beyond a mechanical warning fix.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a different host or elevated path.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Fork PR
options.body: Use the open fork PR only after maintainers confirm warning-only behavior and require current real-behavior proof.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest history signal for exec PTY behavior, fallback behavior, and exec routing semantics.
